newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: Bolivia president agrees transition with successor.
newsitem.headline: Bolivia president agrees transition with successor.

text.p: Bolivia's outgoing President Gonzalo Sanchez de Lozada has agreed with President-elect Hugo Banzer to form 11 commissions to exchange information and ensure an orderly transition of power, government officials said Thursday.

"This is a sign of the democratic maturity that the Bolivian people deserves," Presidency Minister Guillermo Justiniano, who represented the Sanchez de Lozada administration in talks with Banzer, told a news conference.

The accord was delayed a week by disagreement over a government move to force private pension funds to put a large part of their assets in a trust fund, but the government eventually dropped its idea.

The 71-year-old Banzer, Bolivia's military dictator from 1971-78, stood for the right-wing National Democratic Action Party and won elections June 1, although his appointment must still be formally approved by Congress, which meets August 1.
But Banzer has already signed accords with other parties which should guarantee he begins a five-year presidential term August 6.
